name: Claude Agent SDK
question: How do I build an autonomous agent that works with files, code and tools?
summary: The Claude Agent SDK gives you the agent harness behind Claude Code as a library: built-in tools for files, shell and the web, context management, subagents, sessions, hooks that run before and after tool calls, and permission modes. Your own tools are added as MCP servers, including in-process ones. It runs Claude models only, and it is strongest for autonomous work such as operations, research and coding tasks where the agent needs a workspace.
useCases: Agents that read and write files, run code or use a shell

items.detail: Read, Write, Bash, WebFetch and more

steps: Expose your tools through an MCP server
Allow only the tools the task needs
Gate risky tools with a PreToolUse hook
Run in a sandboxed workspace with turn limits
pitfalls: Granting Bash and write access by default
Using it where a simple loop would do
remember: A full harness: allow little, hook the risky calls, sandbox the rest.
caption: Claude models only; Python and TypeScript.

steps.title: Your tools as an MCP server
steps.text: The bank tools are served by an in-process MCP server, the same protocol used for external tools (Panel 8).

steps.title: Allow only what the task needs
steps.text: Only the two bank tools are allowed. The built-in Read, Write and Bash tools exist but are not granted to this agent.

steps.title: A hook gates the risky call
steps.text: A PreToolUse hook on raise_dispute asks for approval and denies the call if the reviewer rejects it.

steps.title: Limit the turns
steps.text: max_turns caps the loop, the same idea as a step budget.

steps.title: A session with the harness
steps.text: ClaudeSDKClient runs a multi-turn session with Claude Code’s context management underneath.

steps.title: Stream the messages
steps.text: Messages stream back as they happen: text, tool calls and results, which you can log or show.

practice.scenario: A fictional broker’s operations team built an agent that investigates failed settlement files overnight: it reads the files, runs reconciliation scripts, queries internal systems through MCP and writes a report. The Claude Agent SDK provided file, shell and web tools out of the box; the team allowed only the tools the task needed, blocked writes outside a working folder with a hook, and ran it in a container.

library.name: Claude Agent SDK
library.what: The Claude Code agent harness as a library: built-in tools, MCP servers, hooks, permissions, sessions and subagents.

practice.note: Only the two bank tools are allowed here; built-in file and shell tools are available but not granted. Check the docs for current hook and option names.

samples.code:
import json
from claude_agent_sdk import (ClaudeAgentOptions, ClaudeSDKClient, HookMatcher,
                              create_sdk_mcp_server, tool)

@tool("get_transaction", "Look up a UPI transaction by its 12-digit UTR", {"utr": str})
async def get_transaction(args):
    txn = await bank.transactions.get(args["utr"])
    return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(txn)}]}

@tool("raise_dispute", "Raise a dispute for a failed UPI debit", {"utr": str, "reason": str})
async def raise_dispute(args):
    ref = await bank.disputes.create(args["utr"], args["reason"])
    return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": f"Dispute {ref} raised"}]}

async def require_approval(input_data, tool_use_id, context):
    if not await approvals.request(input_data["tool_input"]):
        return {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                "permissionDecision": "deny",
                "permissionDecisionReason": "Reviewer rejected the dispute"}}
    return {}

bank_server = create_sdk_mcp_server(name="bank", version="1.0.0",
                                    tools=[get_transaction, raise_dispute])
options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    system_prompt=SYSTEM,
    mcp_servers={"bank": bank_server},
    allowed_tools=["mcp__bank__get_transaction", "mcp__bank__raise_dispute"],
    hooks={"PreToolUse": [HookMatcher(matcher="mcp__bank__raise_dispute",
                                      hooks=[require_approval])]},
    max_turns=8)

async def main():
    async with ClaudeSDKClient(options=options) as client:
        await client.query(QUESTION)
        async for message in client.receive_response():
            print(message)

numericDrill.question: An agent runs 50 tasks a day with 12 tool calls each. If every call needed a manual approval, how many approvals would that be? If only the one dispute-raising call per task is gated, how many approvals a day?
numericDrill.answer: 12 × 50 = 600 approvals a day if everything is gated, which nobody will review properly. Allowing read-only tools and gating only the risky call gives 50: a number people can actually review.

interview.question: When is the Claude Agent SDK a better fit than a lighter framework?
interview.answer: When the agent needs a workspace: reading and writing files, running scripts or shell commands, browsing, and managing long contexts, as in operations, research or coding tasks. It gives you the Claude Code harness with those tools, subagents, sessions and hooks. For a two-tool chat agent it is more than you need.

interview.question: How do you keep an autonomous agent with shell access safe?
interview.answer: Allow only the tools the task needs, gate risky ones with PreToolUse hooks or approval, avoid bypass-permissions mode outside a sandbox, run in a container with no production credentials, cap turns, and log every tool call (Panel 12).

mistakes.mistake: Granting Bash and write access by default
mistakes.fix: Allow only what the task needs
Gate the risky ones so reviews stay meaningful
